# Current-product runtime qualification matrix — planning draft v2

**Status:** proposal for the next qualification design review, not a preregistration or locked workload. Lock a comparison only after its harness, source, build, comparator, and analysis are complete and hashed.

## Scope and baseline

This draft proposes a finite comparison matrix for the current product candidate; it does not freeze the comparisons, add a performance claim, or substitute an earlier runtime snapshot. Before preregistration, finish each proposed harness, lock its source and build, and freeze the analysis. Build both arms from the same current product commit and production dependency lock. The native arm must pass through the mandatory Rust/OXC TSX compiler used by the product Vite build. The React arm must pass through the production React Compiler transform, with its row and board memo-cache proof retained. Both arms use ordinary TSX state APIs and equivalent input data, output values, initial state, row keys, styles, and lifecycle.

The current reusable DOM fixture is `src/browser/product_mixed_harness.ts`, with `src/browser/product_mixed_schedule.ts`, `src/browser/native_product_mixed_arm.tsx`, `src/browser/product_mixed_react_arm.tsx`, and `src/browser/product_mixed_contract.ts`. It fixes N to 128, 512, or 1,024, runs 60 warmups and 240 measured frames, and has eight structural frames that remove 8 rows, insert 8, and rotate 13 retained rows. The latest frozen owner-row-fusion confirmation is `results/product-mixed-owner-row-fusion-confirmation/summary-v3.json`; it passes integrity/correctness but its preregistered median and p95 gates fail at all three sizes. Keep this result and its thresholds unchanged. Its protocol is `product-mixed-owner-row-fusion-confirmation-protocol.md`.

## Finite workload matrix

| Workload | Existing source/evidence to reuse | New harness work needed for a current-product comparison |
|---|---|---|
| Cold mount, first update, teardown | `product_mixed_harness.ts` already records `mountMs` and `disposeMs` and checks writer cleanup. The existing confirmation records these, but does not gate them. | Add a lifecycle mode with fresh roots/pages and separately reported cold mount, first state commit before warmup, and dispose. Preserve output, identity, and cleanup checks. Do not fold these into warm commit samples. |
| Fixed-topology high-frequency | Same three public TSX state slots and `productMixedState` projection in the two product arms. Existing 232 nonstructural measured frames provide context only because the same page also has structural frames. | Add a separate schedule with no collection edits at N=128, 512, 1,024, 4,096, and 10,000. Use fixed dirty counts of 1 row, 32 rows, ceil(1% of N), ceil(10% of N), and all rows. For 32-row and percentage cases, run contiguous and seeded-scattered placements. Hold row data/layout, slot order, and state values equal between arms. Include homogeneous rows and a fixed heterogeneous mixture of at least two compiled component programs/layouts; report whole-cut fallback incidence separately. Let production compiler/runtime choose traversal; no user-facing strategy flag or older kernel implementation. |
| Sparse, bucketed, and dense dirty cuts | Current compiled proof `.cache/compiled-owner-proof/compiled_owner_row_execution_test.mjs` and `results/product-mixed-compiled-owner-rows-pilot/results.json` prove sparse one-cell and dense six-cell semantics, layout order, movement, retirement, reuse, and fallback. They are correctness evidence, not timing results. | Use the same density and placement matrix at all five row counts above, on one underlying state layout. Verify accepted token/slot counts and output parity per frame. Report homogeneous and heterogeneous candidates separately so whole-cut fallback is visible, rather than averaged into a pooled “dense” result. Add a bounded-work diagnostic distinct from timing only if compiler/runtime metadata cannot establish the selected path. |
| Keyed structure only | The current mixed harness supplies the exact 8-remove/8-insert/13-move edit and identity/lifecycle checks. Historical component owner-reuse studies under `results/component-state-owner-reuse-v1/` and `v2/` are not current-product evidence. | Add a current production mode that performs the same keyed edit with no state writes. Keep retained node identity, order, mounts/cleanups, dead setters, and replacement initialization checks. Separate edit-to-commit from ordinary keyed update timing. |
| Mixed state plus keyed structure | Existing frozen product schedule and confirmation: `src/browser/product_mixed_schedule.ts`, `product-mixed-owner-row-fusion-confirmation-protocol.md`, `scripts/collect_product_mixed_owner_row_fusion.mjs`, and `scripts/summarize_product_mixed_owner_row_fusion.mjs`. | No workload rewrite. Keep the existing 30-page schedule, input locks, correctness checks, and stronger preregistered gate as an independent required gate. Any next candidate gets a new immutable source/build lock and fresh confirmation; do not overwrite these records. |
| Async transitions with preloaded data | `src/browser/async_suspense_benchmark.tsx` already compares React Suspense against the runtime using concurrently prewarmed synthetic profile/feed promises, 20 pairs, retained pending UI, and output checks. `results/async-suspense-browser-v1-2026-10-09.json` is historical evidence for that implementation. | Port the workload to the current production package and mandatory Rust/OXC path, and verify the React arm's production React Compiler output. Keep request schedule/data identical and report end-to-visible-result latency plus the synchronous commit interval separately. Check stale-result rejection, pending UI retention, cancellation/transition order, and final output. No network wait should be mislabeled as CPU time. |
| DOM and Three host scope | DOM uses the product fixture above. Current Three API/app source is `src/three_host.ts` and `src/browser/native_three_host.tsx`; `scripts/verify_native_three_host.mjs` and the actual-Three proof referenced by `results/product-mixed-compiled-owner-rows-pilot/results.json` cover 240 five-cell updates, identity/resource retention, and disposal. The app's `Math.sin`-derived vectors currently take fallback paths; this does not prove tuple-kernel eligibility. | Three needs a matched React host arm and timing harness before a parity comparison. Exercise ordinary TSX `position` and `rotation` tuples plus scalar/material properties under identical state updates. The Rust compiler proof must show the exact tuple/property metadata and emitted bindings use the intended specialized path; also retain a negative/fallback case. Do not mutate Three object refs manually to force a fast path. `package.json` has `three` but no React Three renderer, so the comparator/host contract is an explicit implementation gap. Until closed, Three is a separately reported scope/correctness gate, not a pass inferred from DOM or the current native-only proof. |

For new row-count cells, the initial proposal is ten paired fresh page loads per size and workload, alternating native/React order, on the same headed isolated-browser configuration. Use ten pairs for the fixed-size async and Three cells as well. Ten pairs are exploratory for cold mount/first-update/dispose tails: report raw values and p95 descriptively, label quantile precision limited, and do not mark a cold p95 gate resolved. Before a release decision uses cold tails, preregister a larger independent-page sample and its quantile-uncertainty method; ten pairs must not be presented as adequate tail precision. Warm commit samples remain nested within page loads and are summarized page by page. Keep the already frozen mixed confirmation at its original five pairs per size and 30 pages. If collection cost forces fewer page replicates in a new cell, mark p95 precision limited and do not silently pool frames as independent page replications.

## Reporting and decision rules

Report each workload/size/arm separately: cold mount, first post-mount commit, warm ordinary-frame median and p95, structural-frame median and p95 where applicable, dispose time, page-level lifecycle checks, and paired native/React ratios. For async, also report user-visible completion latency and the final synchronous commit duration as separate measures. Never average raw frame samples across pages before computing page medians or page p95s.

For every newly declared comparative cell, require the geometric mean of paired native/React page-median ratios to be at or below 1.00 and the median of paired page-p95 ratios to be at or below 1.00. For a single-event cold metric such as mount or dispose, compute the median and p95 over independent paired page observations; do not invent a within-page p95. The fixed-topology high-frequency workload must additionally show a clear win: paired geometric-mean median ratio at or below 0.80 at two or more sizes, with median paired p95 ratio at or below 1.00 at every size. The unchanged owner-row-fusion confirmation gate remains stricter in its own preregistered form: paired geometric mean of page-median ratios at or below 0.80 at two or more sizes and median paired p95 ratio at or below 1.10 at every size. Both are required; the newer parity criteria do not weaken or rewrite that existing gate.

Keep paired page loads as the replication unit. For each pair, a React denominator below five times the maximum of the preregistered timer quantum and both paired post-disposal quanta is **unresolved**. Preserve the pair and report it as unresolved; do not substitute a run, discard it, or call a sub-resolution ratio a win. Cold mount/dispose comparisons use the same fresh-page pairing and resolution check.

The frame `commitMs` measure is synchronous work inside `controller.step`; it includes TSX rendering, projection, and host commit that runs synchronously in that call, but excludes browser layout, paint, and presentation. A CDP CPU profile started at `about:blank` spans module loading, mount, warmups, measured frames, inspection, and disposal. Protocols such as `product-mixed-compiled-owner-rows-cpu-protocol.md` correctly treat this as whole-page sampled attribution, not commit latency or a per-frame causal breakdown. Keep CPU attribution, frame commit timing, and presented-frame/visual responsiveness distinct.

## Next bounded harness task

First implement one unmeasured current-product fixed-topology harness mode over
the five row counts and fixed density/placement cases above, including both
homogeneous and heterogeneous component programs. It should emit correctness,
fallback incidence, and page-level timing records for the existing native and
React arms. Review the Three comparator/host contract as a separate task before
adding that arm. Only after these harnesses and their analysis code exist should
the workload list be frozen into a preregistration. The already frozen mixed
confirmation remains unchanged throughout.

## Integrity and ship gate

Every timing candidate must preserve its complete Rust compiler source/build archive, exact native emitted metadata, React Compiler evidence, five served production asset hashes, harness/schedule hashes, all raw pages, post-run lock, and independent verifier output. No manually supplied descriptor, alternate hand-authored runtime path, dev server build, historical snapshot, or old kernel result may stand in for the shipping package. Require all correctness, identity, cleanup, stale-write, reentry, and fallback assertions before reading the timing verdict.

Release evidence requires every matrix row marked as a comparative workload to meet parity for both median and p95, the fixed-topology win above, and the unchanged stronger mixed-confirmation gate. Three remains a documented qualification gap until its matched React arm and current-product timing record exist. Any unresolved timer cell, missing current compiler evidence, failed lifecycle/correctness check, or absent workload blocks the broad cross-workload claim; report exact scope instead of generalizing from a passing subset.
